standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic weekly planning task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: The learner maps out one real upcoming week, using school days plus whatever activities, chores, and personal commitments genuinely apply to their own household, onto a single weekly planning grid, without assuming any commitment that does not actually apply to them.
materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app
learner-local: a calendar or existing schedule information for the week

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain whether seeing the whole week on one page changed how you feel about the week ahead, and name one commitment you almost left off the grid until you thought it through.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Grid completeness: All seven days are filled in with the commitments the learner already knew about, across school, chores, and activities as applicable. | Load analysis: The most-loaded day is correctly identified from the grid and paired with a specific, plausible risk. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner add a second column next to each day estimating how much free time is left after commitments, then rank the seven days from most to least free time and explain the ranking.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic weekly planning task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.elapsedWindow: Up to seven days; use only the check-ins explicitly named in the task
duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

localMaterials.label: a calendar or existing schedule information for the week
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: weekly planning worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: The learner maps out one real upcoming week, using school days plus whatever activities, chores, and personal commitments genuinely apply to their own household, onto a single weekly planning grid, without assuming any commitment that does not actually apply to them.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact weekly planning decision or action.
Model move 2: Think back on a week when you had no written plan.
Model move 3: Draw a grid with the seven days of this week as columns, then fill in every commitment you already know about for each day.

Model check: Grid completeness: All seven days are filled in with the commitments the learner already knew about, across school, chores, and activities as applicable. | Load analysis: The most-loaded day is correctly identified from the grid and paired with a specific, plausible risk.

resources.title: weekly planning action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for weekly planning.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: weekly planning coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: The learner maps out one real upcoming week, using school days plus whatever activities, chores, and personal commitments genuinely apply to their own household, onto a single weekly planning grid, without assuming any commitment that does not actually apply to them.
Coach direction: Think back on a week when you had no written plan.
Learner prompt: Describe one moment recently when you forgot about something you were supposed to do or somewhere you were supposed to be.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: weekly planning complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Draw a grid with the seven days of this week as columns, then fill in every commitment you already know about for each day.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I included school or schoolwork time on every school day.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I included every activity, chore, or appointment I already know about this week, not just the ones I remembered first.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: weekly planning minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain whether seeing the whole week on one page changed how you feel about the week ahead, and name one commitment you almost left off the grid until you thought it through.

Success checks: Grid completeness: All seven days are filled in with the commitments the learner already knew about, across school, chores, and activities as applicable. | Load analysis: The most-loaded day is correctly identified from the grid and paired with a specific, plausible risk.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: weekly planning supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional weekly planning condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Grid completeness: All seven days are filled in with the commitments the learner already knew about, across school, chores, and activities as applicable. | Load analysis: The most-loaded day is correctly identified from the grid and paired with a specific, plausible risk..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

resources.title: weekly planning delivered plan
resources.purpose: Resolves the lesson's named plan so the learner is never directed to a phantom material.
content: Starting information: The learner maps out one real upcoming week, using school days plus whatever activities, chores, and personal commitments genuinely apply to their own household, onto a single weekly planning grid, without assuming any commitment that does not actually apply to them.

Field 1 (t2-p1): I included school or schoolwork time on every school day.
Field 2 (t2-p2): I included every activity, chore, or appointment I already know about this week, not just the ones I remembered first.

Check against: Grid completeness: All seven days are filled in with the commitments the learner already knew about, across school, chores, and activities as applicable. | Load analysis: The most-loaded day is correctly identified from the grid and paired with a specific, plausible risk.

simulationRoute.title: weekly planning — complete fictional route
simulationRoute.directions: Complete the weekly planning task using the fictional condition and invented, non-sensitive details on the delivered independent card.
simulationRoute.completionCondition: Complete the same decision, procedure, evidence, and revision checks as the real-life route. No adult attests that a physical event occurred.

independentTask.privacyAlternative: The learner may use invented names, dates, amounts, organizations, spaces, and circumstances whenever real details are unnecessary or private.

learnerEvidence: one revision when a step changed
evidence.reflectionPrompt: Explain whether seeing the whole week on one page changed how you feel about the week ahead, and name one commitment you almost left off the grid until you thought it through.
observableCriteria: Grid completeness: All seven days are filled in with the commitments the learner already knew about, across school, chores, and activities as applicable.
Load analysis: The most-loaded day is correctly identified from the grid and paired with a specific, plausible risk.

account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

retry.trigger: Start the correction loop when a required step is missing, the reason does not match the condition, a safety or privacy boundary is crossed, or the evidence does not show the stated result.
retry.targetedReteach: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step.
retry.supportedReattempt: Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check.
retry.feedback: Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments.
retry.parallelReattempt: Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt.
retry.exitCriterion: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Grid completeness: All seven days are filled in with the commitments the learner already knew about, across school, chores, and activities as applicable. | Load analysis: The most-loaded day is correctly identified from the grid and paired with a specific, plausible risk.
retry.returnPath: Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u01-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
